prompt: You buy 10 shares at ₹100 and 10 at ₹120. What is your average cost?
You hold 20 shares at an average cost of ₹110 and sell 5 at ₹130. What is the realized P&L (before costs)?
After selling part of a holding, the average cost of the remaining shares…

options.text: Is reset to the sale price

explanation: Selling realizes P&L on the sold shares; it does not change the remaining shares' average cost.

options.text: A paper gain or loss on shares you still hold
Profit already credited from a sale

explanation: It becomes realized only when you sell.

prompt: Which statement about losses is correct?

options.text: An unrealized loss is still an economic loss
A loss doesn't exist until you sell
Holding a loser always recovers it

explanation: Not selling doesn't undo the fall in value.

options.text: You own the asset and gain if its price rises
You sold shares you don't own
You hold it for over a year

explanation: Short positions profit from falls; long positions from rises.

prompt: Why can short selling be especially risky?

options.text: Losses are theoretically unlimited because prices can rise without limit

explanation: A rising price increases the short seller's loss without a cap.

prompt: Shares bought today usually appear first under…

options.text: Positions, until settlement moves them into holdings

explanation: Holdings are settled shares; today's trades show as positions first.
